author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be put right on the visit itself. The correction starts from the stored values, is judged by the booking rules, and ends on the owner's record. Correcting never leaves the pet with a second visit.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction is opened, then the form shows that visit's stored date and description
given a changed date later than today and a description, when the correction is submitted, then that visit carries the new values and the owner's record is shown
given a correction that passes, when it is applied, then the pet holds the same visits as before, one of them changed
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the description is named, and the form is shown again
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the date is named, and the form is shown again
edge case 3: correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet is refused rather than applied
edge case 4: a correction never moves the visit to another pet, and never changes any other visit
non_goals: cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, still declined)
a link to the correction from the owner's record or any other page in this slice
notes: Non-goal change recorded the project's way: a new non-goal ADR (docs/adr/2026-08-31-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md), the narrowed NG-5 row, the preamble note, and a status note on the 2026-08-08 ADR. The ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md is owed by that file's owner — outside this agent's write scope. Two open questions recorded instead of a consultation, per the owner's instruction: the missing visible entry point, and whether a visit whose date has passed can be corrected at all. The owner's request (intake-decision, line 1) fixes the correction's address and reuses the booking form; recording that mechanism is the design stage's job, not the PRD's. Pre-existing doctor failure unrelated to this slice: layout.toml spec_version 0.1.0 vs manifest 0.2.0.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: A third correction flow beside owner correction and pet correction, entirely inside the owner feature package. No new package, pattern, dependency, or module boundary. The write path stays OwnerRepository.save(owner); system-design.md (Overview, Contracts) already records Owner as the aggregate entry point and Pet and Visit as persisted only by cascade from it. The one adjustment: VisitController's @ModelAttribute("visit") producer becomes visit-id aware, exactly as PetController's @ModelAttribute("pet") producer is pet-id aware. Mechanism recorded here because the PRD deliberately omits it. Address: GET and POST on /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, one handler pair in the existing VisitController. View: pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm unchanged, whose form element carries no th:action and therefore posts back to the same URL. Model attribute name stays "visit". Basis for the covering claims: no IDE oracle in this run, so PetController.java:75-87 and VisitController.java:63-81 were read directly rather than resolved through search_symbol; treat that as the weaker basis.
integration_points: VisitController gains a GET/POST pair on the /edit address; the existing /visits/new pair is unchanged in behavior
VisitController.loadPetWithVisit gains an optional visitId path variable and becomes the single producer for both flows
No change to Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, or any template; no new message key, no new route on any other page

patterns.description: @ModelAttribute producer taking @PathVariable(name = "petId", required = false) Integer and branching between a fresh entity and the loaded one. The direct precedent for making loadPetWithVisit visit-id aware; use the same required=false wrapper-type shape.
GET/POST pair on the same {id}/edit address, redisplaying the shared create-or-update view on errors and redirecting to redirect:/owners/{ownerId} on success. The correction flow mirrors this shape.
Single-load producer: one owners.findById call whose Owner is put in the model and whose Pet yields the visit. Keep this shape - do not add a second findById.

risks.risk: LOAD-BEARING. loadPetWithVisit is an unqualified @ModelAttribute, so it runs before every handler in VisitController, including the new edit pair. Its current body does pet.addVisit(new Visit()). Left as is, opening or submitting a correction attaches an extra empty Visit to the pet, which cascade-merge then tries to insert; the @NotBlank description makes that a flush-time constraint violation rather than a silent extra row. This is the single mechanism that breaks 'the pet must not gain an additional visit record'.
risks.mitigation: Make the producer branch on visitId: when it is null keep today's new Visit() plus pet.addVisit(visit); when it is present return the visit already held in pet.getVisits() and do NOT call addVisit. Do not add a second, edit-only @ModelAttribute - two producers for the same attribute name in one controller is worse.

risks.risk: Update-in-place does not fall out of the aggregate by itself; it falls out only if the bound Visit is the very instance inside the model Owner's pet. Pet.visits is @OneToMany(cascade = ALL, fetch = EAGER) with @JoinColumn(name = "pet_id") and Visit inherits an IDENTITY-generated id from BaseEntity, so save(owner) merges a visit that carries an id (UPDATE) and inserts one that does not (INSERT). Binding a detached copy, or re-loading the owner separately, produces an insert.
risks.mitigation: Bind onto the instance the producer returned from the model Owner's pet, then call this.owners.save(owner) with no addVisit call on the correction path. No copy-back helper is needed here: unlike PetController, VisitController loads owner and pet from one findById, so the model owner and the bound visit are one graph. Do not mimic PetController.updatePetDetails.

risks.risk: Acceptance criterion 'correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet is refused'. The (ownerId, petId, visitId) triple is caller-supplied and unverified; the visit form is reachable by URL alone and the application has no authentication (system-design.md Security Context), so the identifier chain is the only guard.
risks.mitigation: Verify the chain in the producer by walking owner -> pet -> visit, which makes both handlers safe by construction. Refuse a visitId absent from that pet's visits with IllegalArgumentException, matching the producer's existing treatment of an unknown ownerId and petId. Keep the @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") untouched: the visit is selected by path only, which preserves the mass-assignment mitigation recorded in system-design.md Threat Model.

risks.risk: Adding a message key for a correction-specific heading or button would break the build. The submit button reads #{addVisit} and 11 locale bundles are held key-identical by I18nPropertiesSyncTest.
risks.mitigation: Reuse pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm unchanged, as the owner directed. The template's existing th:if="${visit['new']}" already drops the 'New' prefix from the heading for a persisted visit, and its previous-visits rows are filtered per iterated visit, so both render correctly on the correction form without edits. The PRD lists the template as a file target; no change to it is required by this design.

risks.risk: The non-future-date rule would be stated twice, once per handler, and could drift.
risks.mitigation: Extract it as a private helper in VisitController during a TDD Refactor step. Small enough to fold into the cycle; not a separate refactor slice.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to judge. Wrote one line to docs/adr/README.md - the missing index row for 2026-08-31-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md, which the product expert correctly flagged as outside its scope and owed by this agent. No docs/system-design.md edit: the Contracts table describes current state, and the VisitController row's purpose text plus its Implements list gain REQ-VISITEDIT-001 at doc-sync, after the code exists. Flagging that obligation here so it is not dropped. Open questions recorded rather than raised as consultations, per the owner's instruction. An ArgumentCaptor on owners.save is the fallback if the direct assertion proves awkward.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: `findVisit` is a linear search implemented as a manual for-each loop with an early return, where the checklist prefers a stream pipeline for this kind of filter/find transformation (Design Principles: 'Stream pipelines preferred over manual loops for transformations'). `pet.getVisits().stream().filter(v -> visitId.equals(v.getId())).findFirst()` reads as a lookup rather than a loop with a hidden exceptional exit, and keeps the not-found branch as a single expression via `.orElseThrow(...)`.
findings.fix: Rewrite `findVisit` using `pet.getVisits().stream().filter(v -> visitId.equals(v.getId())).findFirst().orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("Visit with id " + visitId + " not found for pet with id " + pet.getId() + "."))`.

approved_aspects: `rejectVisitDateNotInFuture` extraction removes the date-rule duplication between booking and correction rather than copy-pasting it, keeping the controller's one existing business-rule deviation from growing a second copy
`VIEWS_VISIT_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FORM` constant removes the three repeated view-name string literals
the `loadPetWithVisit` Javadoc update accurately describes the new dual-purpose behavior and documents the new `visitId` parameter and thrown exception
`processVisitCorrectionForm` binds `owner` with `binding = false`, correctly keeping the owner out of form-target binding since only `visit` is the form target
naming (`initVisitCorrectionForm`, `processVisitCorrectionForm`, `findVisit`) follows existing controller method-naming conventions and carries no prohibited suffixes
test setup additions (`bookedVisit` factory, `otherPet`/`TEST_OTHER_PETS_VISIT_ID`) are readable and the class-level Javadoc on the new fields explains why identity assertions are meaningful

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Pre-existing and out of scope for this change, but worth an owner decision as a follow-up: processNewVisitForm still takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner with binding enabled and then calls owners.save(owner), so a POST to /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/new carrying firstName, lastName, address, city, or telephone params mutates and persists the owner record through a form that never offered those fields. docs/security-principles.md scopes findings to what the change introduces, so this is not a defect of REQ-VISITEDIT-001 - the new handler is the corrected pattern. It is flagged because the two siblings now secure the same concern differently, and because a demonstration application's patterns get copied. The fix mirrors the new code: @ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false).

Supply chain was not verified against the NVD in this review: no OWASP dependency-check plugin is configured in build.gradle (plugins are spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management 1.1.7, graalvm native 1.1.2, cyclonedx 3.2.4, javaformat 0.0.47, nohttp 0.0.11), and this reviewer has no network access. The change set adds and upgrades no dependency, so the resolved surface is unchanged by this slice; closing the NVD check remains a CI or human task, not a blocker here.

The correction route is reachable by direct URL with no authentication, authorization, or CSRF token - the demonstration baseline recorded in docs/system-design.md, not a regression. Worth carrying forward if the follow-up request adds a visible entry point: a linked, state-mutating route makes the missing CSRF token materially easier to exercise than an unadvertised one.
approved_aspects: Object-level authorization holds on the new correction route: loadPetWithVisit re-resolves owner -> pet -> visit per request (owners.findById, owner.getPet(petId), then findVisit iterating pet.getVisits()), so a visitId belonging to another pet or another owner raises IllegalArgumentException instead of being corrected. This satisfies the 'Trusting cross-request state' row of docs/security-principles.md - no identifier is trusted because an earlier request validated it. VisitControllerTests covers the mismatched-visit case.

Mass assignment closed on the new POST: the @ModelAttribute(name = "owner", binding = false) on processVisitCorrectionForm stops request params binding onto the model Owner that owners.save(owner) then persists, and the inline comment states why. The controller-wide @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") still covers the bound Visit, so visit.id cannot be rebound to retarget the update. The implementer's flagged divergence from processNewVisitForm is the secure direction and carries its justification, so it satisfies the Pattern Consistency clause rather than violating it.

Correction updates in place rather than inserting: the Visit returned to the model is the instance already held by the pet, so cascade save writes one row and the pet's visit collection is unchanged in shape. No path exists for a correction to move a visit to another pet - the form's hidden petId param is inert on this handler (Visit has no such property and owner binding is off).

New exception message interpolates only path-derived integers (visitId, pet.getId()). Because visitId is typed Integer, a non-numeric value fails conversion before reaching the message, so no attacker-controlled string can reach the error page that renders exception text. No credential, connection string, or session identifier appears in any new message or log line.

Output escaping unchanged: pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders visit date and description through th:text with Thymeleaf's default escaping on, and the form carries no th:action so the correction posts back to its own URL. No th:utext, no inline script, no request-derived value composing a path or a resource name.

No new dependency, no build.gradle change, no shell execution, no deserialization surface, no file or path handling introduced. The nohttp plugin stays enabled and artifacts still resolve from mavenCentral over TLS.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: prd.md's edge case 4 ('a correction never moves the visit to another pet, and never changes any other visit') has no dedicated assertion. The @BeforeEach fixture builds otherPet with its own visit (TEST_OTHER_PETS_VISIT_ID) specifically to exercise this edge case, and it is used to prove refusal when the visitId belongs to another pet, but no test checks that after a successful correction of the booked visit, otherPet's visit is untouched (same id, date, description). The two other acceptance criteria that are adjacent - 'the pet holds the same visits as before, one of them changed' - are covered, but the cross-pet non-interference is not.
findings.fix: Add an assertion (either in theVisitCorrectionShouldLeaveThePetWithNoAdditionalVisit or a new dedicated test named for the behavior) that otherPet.getVisits() still contains a visit equal in id/date/description to the original 'Someone else's visit' fixture after the correction POST completes.

findings.description: This slice's diff rewrites the @BeforeEach setup (converts owner/pet from locals to fields, adds otherPet) and, in the same edit, introduces a factory method for Visit (bookedVisit(...)) but continues to construct Owner and Pet with raw constructors (new Owner(), new Pet() x2). testing-principles.md's Factory Methods section requires that 'a slice touching a test moves that test's construction behind a factory' - this setup block is touched, and the new otherPet construction is new code added by this slice, so it should not still call the production constructor directly.
findings.fix: Add small factory methods (e.g. createOwnerWithPet() / createPet(id)) alongside the existing bookedVisit(...) factory and route the owner/pet/otherPet construction in init() through them, consistent with the pattern the slice already started.

approved_aspects: Test names follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school and match the PRD's prd-entry test_names field exactly
Four-phase structure with blank-line separation and no phase comments across all six new tests

Real Owner/Pet/Visit domain objects used throughout; the only mock is the pre-existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository (system-boundary), and MockMvc for the HTTP transport - both sanctioned by the brief's mocking policy
verify(this.owners).save(this.owner) asserts a real interaction (persistence call) not already covered by the state assertions on the mutated Visit, so it is not a redundant restatement

theVisitCorrectionShouldBeRefusedWhenTheVisitBelongsToAnotherPet correctly exercises edge case 3 via assertThatThrownBy/rootCause, a genuinely new path (IllegalArgumentException from the identifier-chain walk) with no prior coverage

findings.description: Round-1 finding on raw-constructor use in the touched init() block is only partially fixed. Pet construction now goes through the new petRegisteredWith(owner, petId, visit) factory, but `this.owner = new Owner();` on line 100 still calls the production constructor directly inside the same touched setup method. The implementer's stated deviation rationale (Owner.addPet only appends a still-new pet, so a pet must join its owner before receiving an id) explains why petRegisteredWith takes an Owner parameter and orders addPet before setId - it does not explain why Owner construction itself is exempt from a factory. Nothing about Owner's construction has an ordering constraint: `new Owner()` has no id or associations to sequence, so a trivial factory is not blocked by the reason given. testing-principles.md's Factory Methods section states the rule without a triviality carve-out: 'Tests never call production constructors directly... A slice touching a test moves that test's construction behind a factory.'
findings.fix: Add a small factory (e.g. `private static Owner createOwner() { return new Owner(); }`) and route line 100 through it, matching the pattern already used for bookedVisit(...) and petRegisteredWith(...).

approved_aspects: Round-1 cross-pet non-interference finding (edge case 4) is now fully resolved: theVisitCorrectionShouldLeaveTheOtherPetsVisitUnchanged asserts otherPet.getVisits() containsExactly the original otherPetsVisit instance, plus its id/date/description are unchanged, using named constants (OTHER_PETS_VISIT_DATE/DESCRIPTION) rather than magic literals

The petRegisteredWith(owner, petId, visit) factory is a genuine improvement over the prior inline construction, correctly encapsulates the Owner.addPet-before-setId ordering constraint, and is documented with a javadoc explaining why the order matters
New test follows the same BDD naming school and four-phase structure (blank-line separated act/assert, no phase comments) as the rest of the file
